hints: Look at what type of compound ethanal is and remember that aldehydes are very easy to oxidise, so focus on what happens to each oxidising agent.
Start with acidified dichromate on the left, orange $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ is reduced to green $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ when excess aldehyde is present.
Now link the other two tests to their famous precipitates, yellow triiodomethane for the iodoform reaction and red copper(I) oxide for Fehling's, not the silver mirror of Tollens.
walkthrough:
**Recognise ethanal as a reducing aldehyde**

Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, has the $\text{-CHO}$ group. Aldehydes are readily oxidised to carboxylic acids, so they reduce mild oxidising agents.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$

**Solution 1 from acidified dichromate**

Acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is orange due to $\text{Cr(VI)}$. Heating with excess ethanal reduces it fully to $\text{Cr(III)}$.

$$\text{orange Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \rightarrow \text{green Cr}^{3+}$$
So solution 1 is green. This rules out any option starting with orange.

**Solid 2 from alkaline iodine, the iodoform test**

Ethanal contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group, so it gives a positive iodoform reaction on heating with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$. The product is triiodomethane.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{HCOONa} + 3\text{NaI} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$\text{CHI}_3$ is a pale yellow precipitate. So solid 2 is yellow.

**Solid 3 from Fehling's solution**

Fehling's solution contains blue $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ complex. Boiling with an aldehyde reduces it to copper(I) oxide, $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$.

$$\text{blue Cu}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{red Cu}_2\text{O (s)}$$
So solid 3 is a brick-red precipitate. The silver mirror is only seen with Tollens' reagent, not Fehling's. Green, yellow, red matches one option perfectly.

options.A: Solution 1 green and solid 2 yellow are correct, but solid 3 is wrong. A silver mirror is the positive result for Tollens' reagent ($\text{Ag}^+$ to $\text{Ag}$), not for Fehling's solution which gives red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$.
options.B: This is correct. Excess ethanal reduces orange dichromate to green $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate in the iodoform test, and gives red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate with boiling Fehling's solution.
options.C: All three are wrong in logic. Orange would mean dichromate stayed unreacted, but excess ethanal reduces it to green. Red solid 2 confuses Fehling's with iodoform, and silver mirror confuses Fehling's with Tollens'.
options.D: Solid 3 red is correct, but solution 1 and solid 2 are swapped in concept. Orange would mean no reduction of dichromate, which is impossible with excess aldehyde and heat. Red for solid 2 confuses $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ with $\text{CHI}_3$ which is distinctly yellow.
